premise: forced eviction; hidden-swap-ms not wall clock; Fresh-277 cannot exhibit contention
verdict: Deadline CONFIRMED near-optimal among constants. best_constant gains -2.61% (kv=3500) and -0.49% (kv=5000) of the budget, both under the frozen 3% bar and both negative: tuning the constant out-of-fold HURTS. Even the analysis-only in-sample ORACLE_constant reaches only +7.21% and +0.87%.
mechanism: T = kv is exactly the threshold at which the restore penalty vanishes. A call with L <= kv ends before the trigger, so the policy never fires on it and never pays restore. Lowering T below kv starts charging 0.94*kv on every short call it catches, which at rho=0.94 is close to a full swap cost and swamps the extra hiding time gained on the kv..2kv band. Raising T above kv simply discards hiding time. The optimizer confirms this independently: at kv=5000 it fits exactly 5000 ms in four of five folds.
why_the_3500_cell_is_noisier: At kv=3500 the fitted trigger varies across folds (3850, 5050, 5000, 3800, 3700), so the in-sample optimum does not transfer and the out-of-fold policy loses 36.3 s. The in-sample gain of 7.21% is therefore mostly fold-specific fitting, the same overfit pattern f1cbee3 established for per-key methods, here at one scalar instead of thousands.
testable_implication_not_tested: The mechanism predicts the result is contingent on rho. If the restore fraction were much smaller than the measured 0.94, a trigger below kv would become profitable and the deadline would stop being optimal. rho=0.94 is a measured hardware constant on H100 PCIe, so this is not a free parameter here, but it bounds the generality of the finding to swap-back-expensive regimes.
consequence_for_the_lane: The baseline every negative result was measured against is strong, not a strawman. Combined: constants reach at most 7.2% of the budget even fitted in-sample, and per-key empirical methods reach negative under leave-one-out (f1cbee3). The 1392-1478 s budget is therefore essentially unreachable by any policy class tested in this lane.
literature_note: ThunderAgent's ablation states a simplified fixed-threshold variant achieves 'a significant portion' of its gains without naming the threshold or the share. On this workload the fixed threshold at T = kv is essentially the best constant available, so a fixed-threshold baseline is a STRONG reference rather than a weak one. Continuum reports no fixed-TTL baseline at all, which this result suggests is the comparison most likely to change its reported margins.
